subject: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement, monitoring access, and alerting
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@brightroll.com>

Cc: procurement@brightroll.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement, monitoring access, and alerting

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement at BrightRoll is going through our compliance checklist for any new AI vendor and we have a short set of questions specifically around your SLOs, how you measure them, and what customer access looks like. Attached is our questionnaire (spreadsheet) but I pasted the key items below to speed things up.

1) Definitions: What uptime and latency SLOs do you publish for the hosted API and for Dedicated instances? How do you define the measurement window (rolling 7d/30d/etc)?

2) Instrumentation: What metrics do you collect to calculate SLOs (success rate, p95 latency, request volume)? Are these computed at edge load balancer level or inside the serving runtime?

3) Monitoring & alerting: What alert thresholds do you recommend for production alerting? Can we configure alerts (PagerDuty/Slack/Webhook) from your Console?

4) Customer access: Will BrightRoll get read-only access to dashboards with realtime SLOs and historical retention? If so, what data retention windows and exports are supported?

5) Exceptions & credits: Describe your exception process if SLOs are missed (root cause review, temporary exceptions, credits). Typical procurement wants an outline of timelines and evidence that will be provided.

We'd like to get a written response by EOD Pacific today if possible — procurement wants to keep the deal timeline. If you need more time, please let me know and indicate when.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Procurement Lead
BrightRoll Media

Attachments: BrightRoll_SLO_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Draft answers: SLO measurement & monitoring (for review)

Team — draft below for Jonas to send. Kept it short and procurement-friendly; flagged the two places we should confirm with Product (retention, per-tenant alert provisioning).

(START DRAFT)
1) Definitions / published SLOs:
- Hosted API: 99.9% availability measured monthly, p95 request latency <= 220ms for standard generation paths (single-stream responses), computed over rolling 30-day windows.
- Dedicated: contractual availability targets are 99.95% (depending on committed capacity tier); latency targets are specified per-capacity profile in the Dedicated SLA addendum.
- Measurement windows: rolling 30d primary window; we can provide 7d and 90d slices on request for audits.

2) Instrumentation:
- Metrics collected: request_success (boolean), request_latency_ms (histogram), request_count, error_count, backend_retries, queue_time_ms.
- Location: primary SLO computation uses the serving runtime's aggregated metrics (KV cache + runtime success metrics) enriched by edge load balancer ingress metrics to ensure network-layer failures are captured. We reconcile both sources during monthly reporting.

3) Monitoring & alerting:
- Recommended thresholds: availability alert at 99.97% (30d) for P1, sustained p95 > 300ms for 15m as a P1, and error rate spike (>0.5% of traffic) as P1.
- Customers: Yes — BrightRoll can configure alert destinations through the Redwood Console. We support Webhook, Slack, and PagerDuty integrations and can preconfigure a PagerDuty escalation policy for you.

4) Customer access:
- Dashboards: read-only dashboard access with realtime SLOs (1s granularity for edge metrics, 1m for backend aggregates).
- Retention: realtime metrics retained hot for 90 days, aggregated metrics and histograms retained for 13 months (monthly rollups). CSV/JSON exports available for any retention window in the Console.

5) Exceptions & credits:
- Exception process: on detection we open an incident within 2 business hours, perform a root cause analysis within 10 business days, and share a remediation plan. Temporary exceptions (for known external outages) can be recorded and excluded from SLO calculations after mutual agreement; credits are handled as per the SLA schedule (pro-rated credits for monthly availability misses) and issued within the next billing cycle.

(END DRAFT)

Attachments I'm proposing to include: SLO_Measurement_Overview.pdf (concise explainer), MetricsRetention_Table.csv (detailed retention rows), and a one-click dashboard invite (Dashboard_Invite.png stub).

Action: Laura, please review the "Exceptions & credits" paragraph — we should make sure the timelines align with legal's template. Vivek, confirm retention hot/historical numbers above or suggest edits.

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Observability
